stem: A software company's finance team runs eight AWS accounts for different product teams and wants every account's usage combined into one payer account so the company reaches volume pricing tiers and every team's Reserved Instance purchases benefit the whole company.

choices.text: Turn on AWS Budgets alerts on each of the eight accounts
Enable consolidated billing for all eight accounts under one AWS Organizations payer account
Activate cost allocation tags on each account's resources
Configure an AWS Cost and Usage Report for each account

rationale: Consolidated billing under AWS Organizations rolls every member account's usage into one payer account, which is what lets the company combine usage to reach volume pricing tiers and share the benefit of Reserved Instances purchased by any account. AWS Budgets only watches cost or usage against a threshold and sends an alert; it does not combine usage across accounts or share purchase benefits. Cost allocation tags break spend down by team or project inside a single account's reports; they do not merge billing across accounts. A Cost and Usage Report per account delivers granular line-item data for that account; run separately per account it still leaves usage unconsolidated.
